thread.title: 'T. rex of the sea' discovered in Texas
thread.title_full: 'T. rex of the sea' discovered in Texas

author: Buckeye Reporter
title: 'T. rex of the sea' discovered in Texas
text:
A new species of marine reptile called Tylosaurus rex has been identified by researchers, according to a May 22 announcement. The discovery was discussed by experts including University of Cincinnati Associate Professor Takuya Konishi.
The newly described species, named in reference to Tyrannosaurus rex, is believed to have lived more than 65 million years ago in what is now northern Texas. The animal was about the size of a school bus and belonged to the group known as mosasaurs, which were giant marine reptiles related to modern iguanas and monitor lizards.
Amelia Zietlow from the American Museum of Natural History led the research team that described this ancient predator. The findings highlight ongoing efforts by scientists to learn more about prehistoric marine life, which has gained attention through popular films such as “Jurassic World” and its sequel “Jurassic World Rebirth.”
Konishi, who was not involved in this particular study but has spent over a decade analyzing new mosasaur species, said studies like this can help inform future research in the field. In 2023, he helped describe another new mosasaur species known as the “blue dragon,” which lived approximately 72 million years ago.
As paleontologists continue their work on these ancient creatures, further discoveries may shed light on how these large predators adapted and thrived in prehistoric seas.
